1. Approach and rationale:
   We are to minimize the maximum overlap integral C5 for a step function h(x) in [0,2] with integral 1. The provided parent construction achieves 0.380868. Our goal is to improve this using a multi-resolution, multi-start optimization approach with more sophisticated local search.
   We will:
   - Use multiple resolutions to capture both global and local patterns
   - Employ randomized restarts from diverse initializations
   - Refine solutions using a time-allocated, adaptive local search
   - Use projection to maintain feasibility throughout the optimization
   Limitations are the 1100-second budget and the discrete nature of the evaluation

2. Mathematical specification:
   We treat h as a piecewise constant function defined over n=100, 200, 400, 800 grid points.
   Objective: Minimize C5 = max_k ∫h(x)(1-h(x+k))dx
   Constraints: ∑h_i * dx = 1 and 0≤h_i≤1 for all i
   We use a smoothing technique for the optimization near a candidate solution:
     smooth_obj(h) = log(exp(∫h·(1-h)dx/c_max)) 
   to avoid the max constraint in the objective

3. Implementation procedure:
   a. Initialization:
      i. Start with the provided initial_h_values if available (n=250)
      ii. For other resolutions, use random restarts with grid interpolation
   b. Refinement loop:
      i. For each resolution (100,200,400,800):
         1. Take the best candidate from previous resolution (if any)
         2. Time budget allocation: 
            - n=100: 900 seconds
            - n=200: 900 seconds
            - n=400: 600 seconds
            - n=800: 300 seconds
         3. Use a hybrid optimizer:
            • SLSQP for global search (1000 iterations)
            • Pair search with adaptive step sizes (500 iterations)
            • Simulated annealing (1000 iterations)
         4. Local search uses small grid moves and projections
      ii. Track best candidate by C5 value
   c. Constraints handling:
      • Projection to [0,1] after every move
      • Penalty-driven optimization of the integral constraint
   d. Parameter tuning:
      - Smooth parameter α in objective from 1000 to 100000
      - Step sizes in pair search: [0.05, 0.02, 0.01]
      - Annealing schedule: T0=0.01, T_end=0.0001
      - Population size for restarts: 5-15 initial points per resolution

4. Search choices and variations:
   a. Initializations tested:
      i. Provided parent
      ii. Sine wave pattern (density adjusted)
      iii. Truncated Gaussian function
      iv. Uniform steps with random spacings
      v. Grouped pulse trains in phase and out-of-phase variations
   b. Local search variations:
      i. Only two-point mutations
      ii. Localized segment shifts
      iii. Global random position changes
   c. Resolution selection:
      Primary: 100-800 points (powers of 2)
      Failed resolution abort if time exhausts

5. Compute budget and robustness:
   - Dominant costs: Optimization at 800 points: ~300s
   - Critical time checks: Before solver calls (30% allocation)
   - Memory: Handles up to 800-point arrays
   - Budget detection: Periodic time checks (every 10 iterations)
   - Fallback mechanism: Return best found candidate/n even with incomplete execution
   - Validation checks: 
        i. Project to feasibility before return
        ii. vailidate integral≈1
        iii. Ensure 0≤h≤1
        iv. Check finite C5 value

6. Validation and return contract:
   - Final candidate passes:
        1. Integral check: |sum(h)*(2.0/n) - 1| < 1e-6
        2. Bounds check: all 0≤h[i]≤1 within 1e-6
        3. Recompute C5 once to ensure consistency
        4. Handle empty returns and invalid candidates
   - Returns tuple (h_values, C5_bound, n_points) even if not improved
   - Uses projected_candidate to maintain feasibility
   - Precision management with clipping-based projection
   - Smooth_gradient_approximation is too time-heavy, so we use SLSQP without explicit Gradient mode
